beats.narration_slice: Attention drifts; obvious details slip past.
beats.visual: Layered paper-cut close view of the Red Horned Everyman at a sorting table in an abstract subject-world workspace, looking past a clearly different apple while several nearly identical apples pass under his unfocused gaze; slate-blue fatigue layers surround his head and a faint honey highlight on the brain dims toward the edges.
beats.purpose: show that sleep loss weakens attention so obvious details are missed
beats.visual_fingerprint: host at sorting table + overlooking one mismatched apple + tight eye-level close shot + abstract cream-paper workspace + dim slate fatigue halo + asymmetric apple line crossing foreground
beats.continuity: establishes the tired-brain subject world with the host participating directly in the attention example

beats.narration_slice: Reaction time slows, making mistakes easier.
beats.visual: Top-down paper-cut scene of two hands reaching toward a falling apple, with the correct catching hand lagging behind while the apple knocks into a second object; staggered cream and slate motion silhouettes show delayed response without any text or markings.
beats.purpose: show slower reaction time creating a simple physical mistake
beats.visual_fingerprint: falling apple + delayed reaching hands + overhead composition + isolated tabletop zone + staggered motion silhouettes + collision occurring at lower-right corner
beats.continuity: moves from missed visual information to the next consequence: delayed physical response, while dropping the host face for a more kinetic overhead composition

beats.narration_slice: New memories become harder to store.
beats.visual: Simplified cut-paper brain shown in three-quarter view as glowing honey memory tokens approach a layered hippocampus-like inner pocket, but several tokens slide off the edge instead of settling inside; the background becomes a quiet slate-blue anatomical space.
beats.purpose: show impaired formation and storage of new memories
beats.visual_fingerprint: paper brain + memory tokens failing to enter inner pocket + medium three-quarter anatomical view + slate-blue internal space + honey signal pieces + diagonal flow from upper-left to lower-right
beats.continuity: shifts from outward reaction to an internal brain mechanism, using the same honey-versus-slate visual language

beats.narration_slice: Emotional control weakens, so feelings hit harder.
beats.visual: The Red Horned Everyman stands small and calm-looking in profile while an oversized layered red-amber paper wave representing emotion rises behind him; a thin honey-brain control ribbon that normally contains the wave is visibly frayed and loose.
beats.purpose: show reduced emotional regulation causing stronger emotional reactions
beats.visual_fingerprint: small host profile + oversized emotion wave + side-view full figure + open cream-paper stage + frayed control ribbon + wave dominating the upper frame
beats.continuity: returns the host as a scale reference after the brain diagram, turning weakened regulation into a readable physical metaphor

beats.narration_slice: Hunger shifts toward more calorie-dense foods.
beats.visual: Low-angle paper-cut still life where simple high-calorie food silhouettes occupy the bright honey-lit foreground while lighter foods recede into muted slate layers; the host's hand enters from the side choosing the denser option without showing brands or labels.
beats.purpose: show sleep deprivation biasing appetite toward calorie-dense foods
beats.visual_fingerprint: dense-food silhouettes + reaching host hand + low-angle food close-up + tabletop nutrition zone + honey foreground emphasis + lighter foods shrinking into slate background
beats.continuity: moves from emotional regulation to appetite by keeping the host involved only through a restrained hand choice rather than another face shot

beats.narration_slice: Your immune system gets less recovery time.
beats.visual: Night-themed layered paper body silhouette reclines horizontally while small shield-like immune cells repair tiny gaps across the figure; a large pale clock-shape without markings presses inward, leaving several repairs unfinished as slate-blue layers overtake the warm honey recovery glow.
beats.purpose: show that shortened sleep leaves less time for immune recovery processes
beats.visual_fingerprint: reclining body silhouette + unfinished immune-cell repairs + wide horizontal body composition within vertical frame + deep slate night zone + blank clock shape + recovery glow interrupted mid-body
beats.continuity: leaves the food setting entirely and broadens from behavior to whole-body overnight recovery

beats.visual: Vertical cutaway of a simplified blood vessel with a pulsing honey-red stream pressing more strongly against narrowing paper vessel walls; a small heart sits below as the source, with layered pressure arcs expanding outward but no gauges, numbers, or labels.
beats.purpose: show poorer regulation of blood pressure
beats.visual_fingerprint: blood vessel cutaway + forceful pulse against vessel walls + vertical anatomical macro shot + warm cardiovascular zone + pressure arcs + heart anchored at bottom center
beats.continuity: continues the body-system sequence but changes from whole-body recovery to a tight cardiovascular macro view

beats.narration_slice: Blood sugar control can worsen too.
beats.visual: Paper-cut bloodstream seen as a winding river through a cream anatomical landscape, carrying amber sugar-like hexagonal shapes; several shapes remain crowded in the stream while a nearby cell-shaped paper pocket accepts fewer than expected, suggesting impaired control without labels.
beats.visual_fingerprint: winding bloodstream river + crowded sugar shapes + oblique wide anatomical landscape + cream-and-slate metabolic zone + underfilled cell pocket + serpentine composition from bottom-left to top-right
beats.continuity: stays inside body physiology but switches from pressure force in a vessel to metabolic traffic through a broader anatomical landscape

beats.narration_slice: Repeated short sleep is linked with heart disease and diabetes.
beats.visual: A repeated row of small layered bed silhouettes recedes into the background like successive nights, converging toward two large foreground symbols: a stressed paper heart and an overloaded metabolic cell cluster, both partially darkened by accumulating slate-blue layers.
beats.purpose: show that repeated short sleep accumulates long-term cardiovascular and metabolic risk
beats.visual_fingerprint: repeating bed silhouettes + heart and metabolic cell endpoints + deep perspective wide shot + abstract timeline corridor + accumulating slate layers + twin risk symbols framing the foreground
beats.continuity: connects the two preceding physiology beats into a longer-term repeated-sleep pattern rather than another single-system close-up

beats.narration_slice: Caffeine can mask sleepiness, but cannot replace sleep.
beats.visual: The Red Horned Everyman sits upright beside a plain unbranded paper cup, his eyes temporarily ringed by a small honey alertness glow while a larger translucent slate-blue sleep-debt shadow remains attached behind his body; a distant bed silhouette stays visibly separate and untouched.
beats.purpose: show caffeine temporarily hiding sleepiness without restoring lost sleep
beats.visual_fingerprint: host with plain cup + small alertness glow versus large sleep-debt shadow + medium seated three-quarter shot + quiet break area + distant bed symbol + opposing foreground and background states
beats.continuity: returns the host after the long-term risk montage to clarify a common attempted workaround in a simple personal scene

beats.narration_slice: Most adults need at least seven hours nightly.
beats.visual: Calm wide paper-cut night scene of an adult silhouette sleeping in a bed beneath seven small unmarked moon-phase-like paper discs arranged as a purely visual rhythm, with warm honey recovery light returning across the body and slate fatigue layers receding toward the frame edges.
beats.purpose: show the recommended nightly sleep duration for most adults and end on restored recovery
beats.visual_fingerprint: sleeping adult silhouette + seven abstract moon discs + wide serene bedroom composition + subdued night setting + returning honey recovery glow + centered bed with symmetrical overhead rhythm
beats.continuity: resolves the caffeine contrast by showing actual sleep as the restorative endpoint, using a calmer wider composition for the final body beat
